newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke hints rates on hold until election-paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke hints rates on hold until election-paper.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke will signal later on Monday that UK rates will stay on hold until the election, the Financial Times said.
The paper said Clarke will use a speech to the British Retail Consortium to put the case for leaving rates unchanged at 6.0 percent, pointing to benign inflationary pressures.

Clarke will say he is, "reassured by the exceptional lack of inflationary pressures in the pipeline -- from producer prices that are at their lowest since the late 1960s, to moderate earnings and (pay) settlement figures" in the speech.
The election must be held by May.
The pound's recent strength has also put a brake on the economy, Clarke will say.
The FT said Clarke will also use the speech to play down the disagreement with Governor of the Bank of England Eddie George. George thinks rates should rise by a quarter point.
